redCandidate.publicEntry: scripts/workflow-diagnostic-ab.mjs through its public Node CLI test
redCandidate.setup: The focused local-only test creates one temporary non-GAIA task manifest and one temporary diagnostic configuration. It asks the public CLI for --dry-run, which must resolve the two committed AGENTS.md policy sources, verify the local task digest, and emit an isolated single-client summary. The test has no model client, browser, MCP server, network request, credential, or GAIA dataset.
redCandidate.expected: The public dry-run CLI exits zero, reports the one task and identical run controls, and exposes distinct SHA-256 digests for c3b9197853bfb93ec264b03a838162cca9a035c4:AGENTS.md and 4a77ad3d0eb0c5e2043bd9aaea91e3107d6210e9:AGENTS.md before a client could be launched.
redCandidate.observed: The focused test exits with code 1 because Node cannot resolve scripts/workflow-diagnostic-ab.mjs; no client process is started.
redCandidate.failureReason: There is no public no-browser diagnostic CLI or policy-source locking boundary. The existing GAIA CLI deliberately rejects --execute and its live runner requires browser preflight, so it cannot supply the requested diagnostic behavior without conflating it with GAIA.
